PullRequest.Title: sessions: add a Canvases section that starts a session with a canvas
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

## Why

In the Agents window, a canvas can only be opened from a chat that has already been started, so trying one means sending a message first. This lets a user start a session from a canvas instead, from a Canvases section in the sidebar.

## What changed

- **agentHost:** a workspace-less draft chat can list its canvases without starting. The runtime launches early, the way a draft is pre-warmed, and nothing is persisted or announced. Opening a canvas in the draft starts it the way a first send would, reusing that runtime. Listing waits briefly for extensions to settle, then lists what registered, so an extension stuck starting can't hide the others.
- **sessions:** `ISessionsProvider.createCanvasDraft` / `ISessionsManagementService.createCanvasDraft` return an unlisted quick chat that lists canvases and opens one, starting the session under the canvas name. The Agent Host provider shares the session-starting code that a first send already runs. Disposing the draft, or a canvas failing to open, leaves nothing behind.
- **sessions:** `ISessionCanvasCatalogService` remembers the last listed canvas types per profile, so the picker fills in immediately.
- **sidebar:** with the new experimental `sessions.list.canvasesSection` setting (off by default), pinned canvases move under a Canvases section, indented one level. Its **New Canvas...** action, on the header's toolbar and context menu, picks a canvas, starts a session with it without a message, pins it and shows it full-page. With the setting off, the sidebar is unchanged.

![Canvases section with two pinned canvases](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ulugbekna/screenshots/main/vscode/canvas-first-sessions/canvases-section.png)

Recording: [New Canvas → Kusto, New Canvas → Session timeline, switch between pins](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ulugbekna/screenshots/main/vscode/canvas-first-sessions/canvases-section-demo.mp4)

## Scope

Workspace-less (quick chat) sessions on the local Agent Host only. A draft with a workspace still waits for its first send, which creates its worktree. Only canvases from user or plugin extensions that open without input are offered.

## Tradeoffs

- The picker lists canvases from a hidden draft rather than a new session-independent host call, which would need a protocol change.
- The section is behind a setting because it changes the sidebar for everyone who has canvases enabled.

## Verification

- `./scripts/test.sh --run` sessions list, canvas catalog, sessions management, session navigation, local Agent Host provider and pinned canvas suites: 1847 passing.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run copilotAgent.test.ts --run agentService.test.ts --grep "canvas|GC-disposed|warm"`: 102 passing, including new tests for listing in a draft, waiting for a late extension, a stuck extension, and consent requested while a draft lists canvases.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run sessionsManagementService.test.ts --grep "canvas draft"`: 2 passing, including disposal while a draft's canvas is unpublished.
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`, `pnpm run oxlint` on the changed files and `pnpm run valid-layers-check`: clean.
- Manually in a Code OSS Agents window on a fresh profile: with the setting off the sidebar matches `main`. With it on, **New Canvas...** lists canvases without any chat, cancelling discards the draft, and picking Kusto then Session timeline starts two sessions without a message, pins both and switches between them. After review fixes, right-clicking the Canvases header offers **New Canvas...**, which opens a Session timeline canvas in a new session.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The new discovery-to-_warmChat call, unconditional warmUp on a new launch, and exact MCP/tool RPCs are traced in code; both existing warm-up tests and the new draft-listing test corroborate issuance. Runtime comments establish lazy MCP startup, and launcher configuration retains enabled root/plugin servers for these non-ephemeral drafts. Actual server startup duration and users' server counts are unmeasured.
Findings.PerformanceResource: SDK-owned MCP server subprocesses/connections and first-turn tool-catalog/memory preparation.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: One rpc.mcp.list and, if not cancelled or claimed first, one tools.initializeAndValidate per newly launched draft. Each MCP list starts the enabled SDK-owned servers after same-name overrides and disablement; for K picker invocations and M such servers, startup work scales with K times M. Forwarded workbench servers may share underlying resources and are not counted as M new subprocesses. Shared CLI-client startup does not coalesce these per-session RPCs. Warm-up is off the awaited discovery path and runs independently across drafts.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Unnecessary server startup and tool-catalog CPU/I/O work, with transient process and memory pressure during canvas selection; repeated picker invocations restart that work.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Provisional draft canvas listing was rejected, and supported listing on an existing chat called liveSession.listCanvases without _warmChat or first-turn warmUp. MCP/tool prewarming belonged to composing a chat intended for a send, not canvas inventory discovery.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Listing an unstarted workspace-less draft now performs first-turn MCP and tool preparation as well as the runtime launch needed for canvas discovery. NewCanvasSessionAction creates a fresh draft on each invocation, so this preparation also happens when the picker is cancelled or used only to discover extensions.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added call at copilotAgent.ts:3730 sends draft canvas discovery through _warmChat. _warmChat:8389-8403 invokes launch.session.warmUp for every new early launch. warmUp at copilotAgentSession.ts:1788-1799 issues rpc.mcp.list and then rpc.tools.initializeAndValidate; the documented invariant immediately above it states that mcp.list starts otherwise-lazy servers. The added listing test at copilotAgent.test.ts:23996 explicitly expects one mcpLists call before materialization.
Findings.Title: Skip first-turn MCP warm-up when discovering draft canvases
Findings.Impact: With the experimental Canvases section enabled and SDK-owned MCP servers configured, merely opening New Canvas starts unrelated server processes/connections and prepares chat tools before any canvas is chosen. Browsing or repeatedly opening and cancelling the picker causes avoidable startup CPU/I/O and transient process/memory pressure, even when the canvas requires no chat tools.
Findings.Evidence: NewCanvasSessionAction.run creates the draft before showing the picker (newCanvasSessionAction.ts:88-99), regardless of the persisted catalog. BaseAgentHostSessionsProvider.createCanvasDraft immediately requests listSessionCanvases (baseAgentHostSessionsProvider.ts:8193). The new _listDraftCanvases invokes _warmChat, which starts warmUp outside the chat queue. CopilotAgentSession.warmUp calls rpc.mcp.list, bringing lazy servers up, then initializes the entire tool catalog including memory preparation. toSessionConfigMcpServers includes root and enabled explicitly projected plugin servers for non-ephemeral sessions (copilotSessionLauncher.ts:136-144); draft sessions are not ephemeral. Cancelling discards the runtime through _discardEarlyLaunch, so the next picker cannot reuse its MCP/tool preparation.
Findings.Recommendation: Separate early runtime launch from first-turn warmUp, allowing canvas-only discovery to reuse/claim an early launch without issuing mcp.list or tools.initializeAndValidate. Keep first-turn preparation on the existing composer/send path; canvas listing can still activate its extensions through the existing canvas RPC.

Scenarios.Scenario: Show the sidebar with the Canvases-section setting disabled or enabled; expand/collapse it and switch pins.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: SessionsList.update composes the tree synchronously. Enabled mode adds one header and up to five existing pin rows, or one placeholder. Rendering does not wait for canvas discovery or start a draft.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Existing listed sessions plus P pinned canvases, with MAX_PINNED_CANVASES=5. Added tree composition is O(P), not proportional to all canvas definitions or all historical sessions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Main-thread tree updates; existing session-change paths use animation-frame scheduling. The new configuration/enabled listeners update directly but fire on feature-state changes, not each frame. Navigation splicing/layout remains guarded by section identity comparison.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing collapse state and pins are reused. The catalog singleton is delayed and is not instantiated merely to render the section. Navigation sections are deduplicated before splice and clientWidth/layout work.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed tree-composition hunks, navigation deduplication, delayed service registration and the pin cap were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No rendering timings were measured; the added section and pin cardinality are tightly bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable rendering regression. The header changes presentation of existing bounded rows without introducing runtime, filesystem or network work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open New Canvas on a cold profile or reopen it with a remembered catalog, including browsing without selecting a canvas.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The picker appears with cached entries immediately. Fresh entries require configuration readiness, eager backend creation and default-chat state, then a queued early SDK-session launch and settled canvas inventory. The three-second deadline bounds extension-settlement waiting, not total launch/RPC duration. MCP/tool warmUp runs outside the chat queue and is not awaited by canvas discovery.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve session configuration, create one backend session, subscribe to its session/default-chat state and request canvas discovery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally one configuration-discovery request, a second configuration request if initial values differ, one createSession, one session subscription and one default-chat subscription per draft. Configuration failure recovery can retry explicitly; no request per canvas.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These operations already served regular quick-chat drafts, but no standalone canvas picker created a hidden draft or requested its canvas inventory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: BackendChat waits for configuration and eager creation/default-chat state. Cached picker entries remain usable while this runs.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire the shared local CLI client, resolve runtime-managed settings, create one SDK session and perform agent/sandbox initialization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one shared client startup for concurrent local callers; one SDK session per draft. Managed-settings resolution is coalesced only for matching in-flight keys, so a new scratch cwd can require a distinct query. Startup assets and optional enabled plugins are resolved on client startup, not per canvas.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same startup machinery was reached by chat materialization/prewarming; provisional canvas listing previously rejected the draft.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: SDK-session initialization must finish before live inventory is available. The picker itself is already visible.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create the scratch directory, resolve customization/plugin assets and canonicalize runtime/extension roots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One scratch directory per draft, plus work for the E selected extension/plugin roots; extension-admission realpath calls are sequential. Shared installed assets are reusable, but distinct drafts still acquire their launch state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These helpers were used for ordinary quick-chat creation and prewarming, not standalone canvas discovery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Scratch/customization setup and extension admission participate in launch readiness.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read central persisted session-enablement state without importing a session database.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cached/coalesced session load per new owner despite several initializeSession callers. An unpersisted draft normally has no stored decisions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing quick-chat initialization already used this service; the new picker adds another draft owner.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Launch waits for authoritative enablement; later callers reuse the session load.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Probe the scratch cwd with git rev-parse to resolve project metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cold repository-root lookup for each distinct scratch cwd; in-flight lookups coalesce by cwd and existing negative results are reusable. A normal scratch directory is not a repository.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same probe occurred during ordinary provisional launch, not a standalone canvas-inventory action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The project promise runs beside launch; materialization later awaits it, while discovery itself does not.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request the runtime's canvas registry and extension inventory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two concurrent RPCs per listing iteration. Retries follow extension/registry changes or the settlement deadline; this is collection-wide inventory, not one RPC per canvas.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing live-chat listing used one pair of inventory RPCs; drafts could not list. The diff adds event-driven settlement retries for draft discovery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Fresh picker entries await the settled or include-starting snapshot.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Validate icon paths/files, read bounded PNG bytes and encode icon data URIs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to C icon loads for each candidate usable snapshot. A warm per-runtime LRU avoids byte rereads for matching mtime/size but still validates filesystem metadata; a fresh picker draft has a fresh LRU. File buffers are bounded by MAX_CANVAS_ICON_BYTES.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same bounded loader served live-chat inventories; the new hidden-draft workflow also reaches it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The inventory response waits for icon transformations. This loader was not changed by the PR.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start otherwise-lazy SDK-owned MCP servers through rpc.mcp.list, then prepare/validate the full first-turn tool catalog, including memory preparation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One mcp.list per newly launched draft and, if still unclaimed/uncancelled, one tools.initializeAndValidate. Actual startup work scales with K times M enabled SDK-owned servers, rather than C canvas definitions. Shared CLI startup does not merge per-session warmUp.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Canvas listing did not call first-turn warmUp. This work belonged to chat composition/prewarming before a send.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the awaited discovery path, but consumes process/connection/CPU/I/O resources while the user browses the picker. Tools are not needed by canvas inventory.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: K picker invocations, E launch extension/plugin roots, C registered canvas definitions and M enabled SDK-owned MCP servers after disablement and same-name overrides. One fresh draft is created per invocation, not per canvas definition. M excludes forwarded servers whose underlying workbench resources can be shared.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each draft's launch is serialized by its own chat lifetime/queue. Different drafts can progress independently. Local drafts share the CLI client and in-flight client startup. Canvas and extension inventory RPCs run concurrently within each iteration; icons are read with Promise.all. No aggregate limiter surrounds per-draft MCP warmUp.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The profile catalog supplies immediate UI but does not suppress draft creation or discovery. Successful discovery replaces rather than appends the catalog; equal normalized entries suppress storage writes, and stored icons are limited to 32 KiB each. CLI startup is shared; managed-settings queries join only while rpc/token/cwd keys match. Each fresh runtime has its own lazy 64-entry icon LRU, including cached invalid PNG results after file checks. Cancelling the draft prevents reuse of its MCP/tool preparation on the next invocation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added call chain, RPC issuance, per-draft ownership and independent chat queues are explicit, and the new listing test expects an MCP list before materialization.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Server counts, transport mix, startup time and exact tool-memory cost depend on the user's configuration. No benchmark numbers are assumed. The feature is experimental and disabled by default.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported one medium-severity eager-work regression: canvas-only discovery unnecessarily runs first-turn MCP/tool preparation. Runtime launch and authoritative inventory themselves are required by the chosen implementation and are not separately reported.

Scenarios.Scenario: Choose a canvas, start its session, wait for publication, pin it and show its full-page view.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Open waits for backendChat and queued materialization; a compatible early launch is claimed rather than recreated. Session metadata persistence and provider graduation precede publication observation. The service waits up to ten seconds for the instance, then holds observation until pin/show finishes. Consent can legitimately wait for user input. The first visible page must create/load its browser model.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist session metadata/deferred SDK execution and announce the durable session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Session-scoped persistence, not one transaction per canvas-definition candidate; supplied metadata is batched. Baseline checkpoint work is launched separately.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A first send performed this persistence; opening a workspace-less draft canvas could not previously materialize it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Durability/materialization must complete before the provider returns the committed session.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronize idle permission mode, inspect the selected extension and open the requested canvas instance, including consent continuation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initial open per selected instance, with consent responses continuing the existing operation rather than opening again. Extension/permission reads are operation-scoped, not per available canvas.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These same RPCs handled canvases in already-started chats. The diff permits them to start a workspace-less draft.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for opening and consent; waits are bounded except the user's decision.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh the host's full session listing, reconcile adapters and rename the committed session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full list when no refresh is active; concurrent refresh callers share the active computation and one trailing request. Host computation bulk-reads central catalogs for N eligible visible sessions, groups prewarming by fallback provider and limits per-session fallback work to four. Rename is one action for the new session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The identical refresh/wait and optional rename already ran for first-send graduation. The refactor preserves that cost; the new canvas-start path shares it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Graduation awaits the effective list before returning the committed session.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Observe session/default-chat membership and canvas-state channels until the selected instance is published.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Refcounted session/chat subscriptions plus one channel for each actual published canvas, normally one in this new session. The returned reference is held only through pin/show, and timeout/service disposal releases it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: An already-visible chat owned these observations. The new hidden session needs an explicit temporary observation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The selected canvas must publish before a usable reference is returned.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Keep the selected canvas observed and create an external Electron browser view for its source.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One pin lease for the selected canvas, with five pins maximum; one browser-model creation per fresh reference/source, joined/reused for subsequent callers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing pin/show used exactly this browser-model path after a canvas was opened in an existing chat. The PR reuses it without changing its allocation or cache policy.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Pin keeps membership alive; browser creation/source loading is needed before the page can display content.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load the selected canvas source in the browser view.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initial document load for the new canvas; content-dependent subresource requests are renderer-owned. Same-source browser models are reused; no loads occur for every picker item.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same canvas source was loaded when shown through existing canvas/pin actions; the new action reaches that existing path after selection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Content loading affects first page readiness, not inventory discovery or sidebar rendering.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One new session and selected canvas per action; typically one published canvas, with subscriptions scaling with actual chat canvas membership. Graduation's full listing scales with visible registered history N, but central-catalog rows avoid provider/session-database fallback. Persistent pins remain capped at five.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Same-chat launch/materialization is serialized. Discovery and early MCP warmUp can still be in flight beside opening. Provider session refreshes serialize per connection with one coalesced trailing refresh. Host list computations coalesce by mode/registry epoch; catalog misses use a four-way fallback limiter. Canvas observations use refcounted subscriptions; same-reference/source browser model creation is coalesced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Early-launch claim validates model/trust/customization state and replaces only stale launches. Session/client state is shared through refcounts. The full-list pipeline uses authoritative central catalogs, hides excluded external rows before metadata work and groups fallback prewarming by provider. Browser models and pending creations are reused by reference/source. The returned observation is explicitly released after pinning/showing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for ordering, shared launch, refresh grouping, temporary observation ownership and browser-model reuse; runtime/content durations are unmeasured.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: History size and fallback eligibility determine graduation cost; canvas document size and extension behavior determine page readiness. No new per-history-row boundary mechanism is claimed.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional high-confidence regression. Existing first-send graduation, live-canvas observation and browser presentation are reused. Their unavoidable costs are not treated as newly broken solely because the new workflow reaches them.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cancel or dismiss the picker, choose Discover More, fail a canvas open, retry, or dispose the service while publication is pending.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Picker dismissal returns immediately and disposes the draft. In-flight SDK create is not abortable, so chat disposal waits for queued launch completion before destroying the early runtime. Failed opens discard the ungraduated session. Publication waiting ends on service cancellation or its ten-second timer.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Release subscriptions and issue disposeSession for an unused backend draft.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One discard transition per draft; settled/opening state prevents repeated disposal by the action. Actual backend teardown follows that draft's queue.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Unused ordinary quick-chat drafts already used this cleanup. The new action creates/discards its own hidden draft.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the picker-dismissal critical path; it can wait for the in-flight launch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Destroy the live session, stop MCP resources, cancel pending auth requests and delete unclaimed SDK state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One owned early launch per draft, destroyed once; storage-client deletion is session-scoped. Local drafts share the existing client, not a new CLI subprocess per deletion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same early-launch cleanup handled abandoned composed drafts. The new picker also owns and releases an early launch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cleanup awaits queued launch/destruction but does not block picker dismissal.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Remove the abandoned session's owned scratch state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One distinct scratch directory per discarded quick-chat draft.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing quick-chat deletion already cleaned its scratch directory; the picker adds another such draft.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Part of asynchronous session disposal, not required for closing the picker.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: K abandoned/retried picker drafts, each with one backend/session lifetime and the enabled resources described in discovery. No accumulating pin lease is created by picker cancellation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Cleanup is serialized behind work for that chat, not globally. Different abandoned drafts may have overlapping launch/cleanup. MCP warmUp can already have issued its request before cleanup; its token prevents later tool initialization when cancellation wins.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The persistent catalog may be refreshed by a listing that completes after dismissal, but it replaces a bounded-field snapshot. Cancelled runtime/MCP/tool state is discarded, so it is not a reusable cache for the next picker. Publication observations/timers are disposed on failure or service cancellation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: draft-state ownership, NewSession disposal, queued early-launch destruction, cancellation checks and observation release were followed.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Launch and remote-server shutdown durations vary. Static evidence establishes unnecessary startup churn but not persistent leakage or a numeric peak process count.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate cleanup-lifecycle finding. Cleanup handles remain reachable and are released. Repeated unnecessary MCP startup before cancellation is covered by the single eager-work finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Send the first normal chat request, list canvases in an already-started chat, or keep a canvas-started session after its first materialization.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The first-send path still sends, seeds its title and enters the shared graduation helper. Existing non-draft canvas listing follows the previous resolver/listCanvases path. Materialization now marks the durable session used so unused-draft GC cannot delete it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the request, refresh the committed-session listing and optionally rename the session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Same send and grouped full-refresh operations as before extraction; no newly introduced per-item call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This logic was inline in the first-send method with the same listing/rename ordering and boundary cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The same first-send commit path waits on the effective listing and optional rename.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read live canvas/extension inventory and existing bounded icons for a started chat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Same collection-wide pair of inventory RPCs and icon reads as before; the draft-specific settlement path is not taken.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing inventory callers wait as before, and released continuity still avoids unnecessary cold launch.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One first-send graduation per session, existing history N for the same full refresh, and actual canvas inventory C. Marking used updates one existing state entry.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing per-chat queues, provider listing coalescing and host metadata-fallback limiter are preserved. The rename/selection handoff remains after commit. No new independent runtime launch occurs for existing non-draft inventory.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Configuration/model/agent selections are preserved through the extracted helper as before. Existing inventory/cache and idle/release lifetimes are unchanged. The used marker intentionally retires only unused-draft collection eligibility.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: before/after graduation hunks and the distinct draft branch were compared, along with GC state ownership.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Normal history and inventory sizes vary; the refactor does not establish a new scaling cost. No numeric impact is attributed to the used-state marker.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional performance regression or qualifying performance-regression fix. Preventing accidental GC of an intentional canvas-first session is a lifecycle/correctness change, not evidence of a removed performance regression.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the distinct performance-review pass against base 817607ae52b88ef6021bb456e5995b6367e1b481 and head 202280de2d66d23568ce56a17fe25c588c4e7d0c. Inspected the complete 26-file inventory and every diff page; no binary or unreviewable changed files. Submitted one medium, high-confidence eager-work finding for first-turn MCP/tool warmUp on hidden-draft canvas discovery. Accounted for sidebar rendering, cold/warm picker discovery, selection/materialization/graduation, pin/browser display, cancellation/failure cleanup and existing first-send/live-inventory paths. Preserved grouped/coalesced call counts and separated static mechanism confidence from unmeasured magnitude. No qualifying performance fix provenance was identified.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
